verses.zh: 在凯撒利亚有一个人，名叫哥尼流，是「意大利营」的百夫长。
verses.en: Now there was a man in Caesarea[NOTE:1] named Cornelius, a centurion[NOTE:2] of what was known as the Italian Cohort.[NOTE:3]
notes: Caesarea was a city on the coast of Palestine south of Mount Carmel (not Caesarea Philippi). It was known as “Caesarea by the sea” (BDAG 499 s.v. Καισάρεια 2). Largely Gentile, it was a center of Roman administration and the location of many of Herod the Great’s building projects (Josephus, Ant. 15.9.6 [15.331-341]).map For location see Map2-C1; Map4-B3; Map5-F2; Map7-A1; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

A centurion was a noncommissioned officer in the Roman army or one of the auxiliary territorial armies, commanding a centuria of (nominally) 100 men. The responsibilities of centurions were broadly similar to modern junior officers, but there was a wide gap in social status between them and officers, and relatively few were promoted beyond the rank of senior centurion. The Roman troops stationed in Judea were auxiliaries, who would normally be rewarded with Roman citizenship after 25 years of service. Some of the centurions throughout the region may have served originally in the Roman legions (regular army) and thus gained their citizenship at enlistment. Others may have inherited it, like the apostle Paul did (cf. Acts 22:28).

A cohort was a Roman military unit of about 600 soldiers, one-tenth of a legion (BDAG 936 s.v. σπεῖρα). The Italian Cohort has been identified as cohors II Italica which is known to have been stationed in Syria in a.d. 88.

verses.zh: 他是个虔诚人，他和全家都敬畏　神，多多周济百姓，常常祷告　神。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] was a devout, God-fearing man,[NOTE:2] as was all his household; he did many acts of charity for the people[NOTE:3] and prayed to God regularly.
notes: In the Greek text this represents a continuation of the previous sentence. Because of the tendency of contemporary English to use shorter sentences, a new sentence was begun here in the translation.

The description of Cornelius as a devout, God-fearing man probably means that he belonged to the category called “God-fearers,” Gentiles who worshiped the God of Israel and in many cases kept the Mosaic law, but did not take the final step of circumcision necessary to become a proselyte to Judaism. See further K. G. Kuhn, TDNT 6:732-34, 43-44, and Sir 11:17; 27:11; 39:27.
Or “gave many gifts to the poor.” This was known as “giving alms,” or acts of mercy (Sir 7:10; BDAG 315-16 s.v. ἐλεημοσύνη).

verses.zh: 有一天，约在申初，他在异象中明明看见　神的一个使者进去，到他那里，说：「哥尼流。」
verses.en: About three o’clock one afternoon[NOTE:1] he saw clearly in a vision an angel of God[NOTE:2] who came in[NOTE:3] and said to him, “Cornelius.”
notes: Grk “at about the ninth hour of the day.” This would be the time for afternoon prayer.

Or “the angel of God.” Linguistically, “angel of God” is the same in both testaments (and thus, he is either “an angel of God” or “the angel of God” in both testaments). For arguments and implications, see ExSyn 252; M. J. Davidson, “Angels,” DJG, 9; W. G. MacDonald argues for “an angel” in both testaments: “Christology and ‘The Angel of the Lord’,” Current Issues in Biblical and Patristic Interpretation, 324-35.
The participles εἰσελθόντα (eiselthonta) and εἰπόντα (eiponta) are accusative, and thus best taken as adjectival participles modifying ἄγγελον (angelon): “an angel who came in and said.”

verses.zh: 哥尼流定睛看他，惊怕说：「主啊，甚么事呢？」天使说：「你的祷告和你的周济达到　神面前，已蒙记念了。
verses.en: Staring at him and becoming greatly afraid, Cornelius[NOTE:1] replied,[NOTE:2] “What is it, Lord?” The angel[NOTE:3] said to him, “Your prayers and your acts of charity[NOTE:4] have gone up as a memorial[NOTE:5] before God.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Cornelius) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “said,” but in response to the angel’s address, “replied” is better English style.
Grk “he”; the referent (the angel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “your gifts to the needy.”
The language used in the expression gone up as a memorial before God parallels what one would say of acceptable sacrifices (Ps 141:2; Sir 35:6; 50:16).

verses.zh: 现在你当打发人往约帕去，请那称呼彼得的西门来。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] send men to Joppa[NOTE:2] and summon a man named Simon,[NOTE:3] who is called Peter.
notes: Grk “And now.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Joppa was a seaport on the Philistine coast, in the same location as modern Jaffa.
Grk “a certain Simon.”

verses.zh: 他住在海边一个硝皮匠西门的家里，房子在海边上。」
verses.en: This man is staying as a guest with a man named Simon, a tanner,[NOTE:1] whose house is by the sea.”
notes: Or “with a certain Simon Berseus.” Although most modern English translations treat βυρσεῖ (bursei) as Simon’s profession (“Simon the tanner”), it is possible that the word is actually Simon’s surname (“Simon Berseus” or “Simon Tanner”). BDAG 185 s.v. βυρσεύς regards it as a surname. See also MM 118.

verses.zh: 向他说话的天使去后，哥尼流叫了两个家人和常伺候他的一个虔诚兵来，
verses.en: When the angel who had spoken to him departed, Cornelius[NOTE:1] called two of his personal servants[NOTE:2] and a devout soldier from among those who served him,[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Cornelius) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Or “domestic servants.” The Greek word here is οἰκέτης (oiketēs), which technically refers to a member of the household, but usually means a household servant (slave) or personal servant rather than a field laborer.

The meaning of the genitive participle προσκαρτερούντων (proskarterountōn) could either be “a soldier from the ranks of those who served him” (referring to his entire command) or “a soldier from among his personal staff” (referring to a group of soldiers who were his personal attendants). The translation “from among those who served him” is general enough to cover either possibility.

verses.zh: 把这事都述说给他们听，就打发他们往约帕去。
verses.en: and when he had explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.

verses.zh: 第二天，他们行路将近那城。彼得约在午正，上房顶去祷告，
verses.en: About noon[NOTE:1] the next day, while they were on their way and approaching[NOTE:2] the city, Peter went up on the roof[NOTE:3] to pray.
notes: Grk “about the sixth hour.”
The participles ὁδοιπορούντων (hodoiporountōn, “while they were on their way”) and ἐγγιζόντων (engizontōn, “approaching”) have been translated as temporal participles.

Went up on the roof. Most of the roofs in the NT were flat roofs made of pounded dirt, sometimes mixed with lime or stones, supported by heavy wooden beams. They generally had an easy means of access, either a sturdy wooden ladder or stone stairway, sometimes on the outside of the house.

verses.zh: 觉得饿了，想要吃。那家的人正预备饭的时候，彼得魂游象外，
verses.en: He became hungry and wanted to eat, but while they were preparing the meal, a trance came over him.[NOTE:1]
notes: The traditional translation, “he fell into a trance,” is somewhat idiomatic; it is based on the textual variant ἐπέπεσεν (epepesen, “he fell”) found in the Byzantine text but almost certainly not original.

verses.zh: 看见天开了，有一物降下，好像一块大布，系着四角，缒在地上，
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] saw heaven[NOTE:2] opened[NOTE:3] and an object something like a large sheet[NOTE:4] descending,[NOTE:5] being let down to earth[NOTE:6] by its four corners.
notes: Grk “And he.” Because of the length of the Greek sentence, the conjunction καί (kai) has not been translated here. Instead a new English sentence is begun.
Or “the sky” (the same Greek word means both “heaven” and “sky”).
On the heavens “opening,” see Matt 3:16; Luke 3:21; Rev 19:11 (cf. BDAG 84 s.v. ἀνοίγω 2). This is the language of a vision or a revelatory act of God.
Or “a large linen cloth” (the term was used for the sail of a ship; BDAG 693 s.v. ὀθόνη).
Or “coming down.”
Or “to the ground.”

verses.zh: 里面有地上各样四足的走兽和昆虫，并天上的飞鸟；
verses.en: In it[NOTE:1] were all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles[NOTE:2] of the earth and wild birds.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “in which.” The relative pronoun was replaced by the pronoun “it,” and a new sentence was begun in the translation at this point to improve the English style.

Or “snakes.” Grk “creeping things.” According to L&N 4.51, in most biblical contexts the term (due to the influence of Hebrew classifications such as Gen 1:25-26, 30) included small four-footed animals like rats, mice, frogs, toads, salamanders, and lizards. In this context, however, where “creeping things” are contrasted with “four-footed animals,” the English word “reptiles,” which primarily but not exclusively designates snakes, is probably more appropriate. See also Gen 6:20, as well as the law making such creatures unclean food in Lev 11:2-47.

Grk “the birds of the sky” or “the birds of the heaven”; the Greek word οὐρανός (ouranos) may be translated either “sky” or “heaven,” depending on the context. The idiomatic expression “birds of the sky” refers to wild birds as opposed to domesticated fowl (cf. BDAG 809 s.v. πετεινόν).

verses.zh: 又有声音向他说：「彼得，起来，宰了吃！」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] a voice said[NOTE:2] to him, “Get up, Peter; slaughter[NOTE:3] and eat!”
notes: Grk “And there came.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “a voice to him”; the word “said” is not in the Greek text but is implied.
Or “kill.” Traditionally θῦσον (thuson) is translated “kill,” but in the case of animals intended for food, “slaughter” is more appropriate.

verses.zh: 彼得却说：「主啊，这是不可的！凡俗物和不洁净的物，我从来没有吃过。」
verses.en: But Peter said, “Certainly not, Lord, for I have never eaten anything defiled and ritually unclean!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Possibly there is a subtle distinction in meaning between κοινός (koinos) and ἀκάθαρτος (akathartos) here, but according to L&N 53.39 it is difficult to determine precise differences in meaning based on existing contexts.sn Peter insisted he would not violate the law by eating anything defiled and ritually unclean. These food laws were one of the practices that distinguished Jews from their Gentile neighbors. The practice made table fellowship with Gentiles awkward. For an example of Jewish attitudes to this, see Dan 1:8-16; 1 Macc 1:41-64; Letter of Aristeas 142; Tacitus, History 5.5.

verses.zh: 第二次有声音向他说：「　神所洁净的，你不可当作俗物。」
verses.en: The voice[NOTE:1] spoke to him again, a second time, “What God has made clean, you must not consider[NOTE:2] ritually unclean!”[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “And the voice.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Or “declare.”
For the significance of this vision see Mark 7:14-23; Rom 14:14; Eph 2:11-22. God directed this change in practice.

verses.zh: 这样一连三次，那物随即收回天上去了。
verses.en: This happened three times, and immediately the object was taken up into heaven.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “into the sky” (the same Greek word means both “heaven” and “sky”).

verses.zh: 彼得心里正在猜疑之间，不知所看见的异象是甚么意思。哥尼流所差来的人已经访问到西门的家，站在门外，
verses.en: Now while Peter was puzzling over[NOTE:1] what the vision he had seen could signify, the men sent by Cornelius had learned where Simon’s house was[NOTE:2] and approached[NOTE:3] the gate.
notes: Or “was greatly confused over.” The term means to be perplexed or at a loss (BDAG 235 s.v. διαπορέω).
Grk “having learned.” The participle διερωτήσαντες (dierōtēsantes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

BDAG 418 s.v. ἐφίστημι 1 has “ἐπί τι approach or stand by someth. (Sir 41:24) Ac 10:17.”sn As Peter puzzled over the meaning of the vision, the messengers from Cornelius approached the gate. God’s direction here had a sense of explanatory timing.

verses.zh: 喊着问：「有称呼彼得的西门住在这里没有？」
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] called out to ask if Simon, known as Peter,[NOTE:2] was staying there as a guest.
notes: Grk “and.” Because of the length of the Greek sentence, the conjunction καί (kai) has not been translated here. Instead a new English sentence is begun by supplying the pronoun “they” as the subject of the following verb.
Grk “Simon, the one called Peter.” This qualification was necessary because the owner of the house was also named Simon (Acts 9:43).

verses.zh: 彼得还思想那异象的时候，圣灵向他说：「有三个人来找你。
verses.en: While Peter was still thinking seriously about[NOTE:1] the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Look! Three men are looking for you.
notes: The translation “think seriously about” for διενθυμέομαι (dienthumeomai) is given in L&N 30.2. Peter was “pondering” the vision (BDAG 244 s.v.).

verses.zh: 起来，下去，和他们同往，不要疑惑，因为是我差他们来的。」
verses.en: But get up,[NOTE:1] go down, and accompany them without hesitation[NOTE:2] because I have sent them.”
notes: Grk “But getting up, go down.” The participle ἀναστάς (anastas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
The term means “without doubting” or “without deliberation.” It is a term of conscience and discernment. In effect, Peter is to listen to them rather than hesitate (BDAG 231 s.v. διακρίνω 6).

verses.zh: 于是彼得下去见那些人，说：「我就是你们所找的人。你们来是为甚么缘故？」
verses.en: So Peter went down[NOTE:1] to the men and said, “Here I am,[NOTE:2] the person you’re looking for. Why have you come?”
notes: Grk “Peter going down to the men, said.” The participle καταβάς (katabas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Grk “Behold, it is I whom you seek,” or “Behold, I am the one you seek.” “Here I am” is used to translate ἰδοὺ ἐγώ εἰμι (idou egō eimi).

verses.zh: 他们说：「百夫长哥尼流是个义人，敬畏　神，为犹太通国所称赞。他蒙一位圣天使指示，叫他请你到他家里去，听你的话。」
verses.en: They said, “Cornelius the centurion,[NOTE:1] a righteous[NOTE:2] and God-fearing man, well spoken of by the whole Jewish nation,[NOTE:3] was directed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear a message[NOTE:4] from you.”
notes: See the note on the word centurion in 10:1.
Or “just.”

The long introduction of Cornelius by his messengers is an attempt to commend this Gentile to his Jewish counterpart, which would normally be important to do in the culture of the time.tn The phrase τοῦ ἔθνους τῶν ᾿Ιουδαίων (tou ethnous tōn Ioudaiōn) is virtually a technical term for the Jewish nation (1 Macc 10:25; 11:30, 33; Josephus, Ant. 14.10.22 [14.248]). “All the Jewish people,” while another possible translation of the Greek phrase, does not convey the technical sense of a reference to the nation in English.
Grk “hear words.”

verses.zh: 彼得就请他们进去，住了一宿。次日，起身和他们同去，还有约帕的几个弟兄同着他去；
verses.en: So Peter[NOTE:1] invited them in and entertained them as guests.On the next day he got up and set out[NOTE:2] with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa[NOTE:3] accompanied him.
notes: When Peter entertained them as guests, he performed a culturally significant act denoting acceptance.tn Grk “he”; the referent (Peter) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “went forth.”
Some of the brothers from Joppa. As v. 45 makes clear, there were Jewish Christians in this group of witnesses.

verses.zh: 又次日，他们进入凯撒利亚，哥尼流已经请了他的亲属密友等候他们。
verses.en: The following day[NOTE:1] he entered Caesarea.[NOTE:2] Now Cornelius was waiting anxiously[NOTE:3] for them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
notes: Grk “On the next day,” but since this phrase has already occurred in v. 23, it would be redundant in English to use it again here.
For location see Map2-C1; Map4-B3; Map5-F2; Map7-A1; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.sn Caesarea was a city on the coast of Palestine south of Mount Carmel (not Caesarea Philippi).

Normally προσδοκάω (prosdokaō) means “to wait with apprehension or anxiety for something,” often with the implication of impending danger or trouble (L&N 25.228), but in this context the anxiety Cornelius would have felt came from the importance of the forthcoming message as announced by the angel.

verses.zh: 彼得一进去，哥尼流就迎接他，俯伏在他脚前拜他。
verses.en: So when[NOTE:1] Peter came in, Cornelius met[NOTE:2] him, fell[NOTE:3] at his feet, and worshiped[NOTE:4] him.
notes: Grk “So it happened that when.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.
Grk “meeting him.” The participle συναντήσας (sunantēsas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Grk “falling at his feet, worshiped.” The participle πεσών (pesōn) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
When Cornelius worshiped Peter, it showed his piety and his respect for Peter, but it was an act based on ignorance, as Peter’s remark in v. 26 indicates.

verses.zh: 彼得却拉他，说：「你起来，我也是人。」
verses.en: But Peter helped him up,[NOTE:1] saying, “Stand up. I too am a mere mortal.”[NOTE:2]
notes: BDAG 271 s.v. ἐγείρω 3 has “raise, help to rise….Stretched out Ac 10:26.”

Although it is certainly true that Peter was a “man,” here ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos) has been translated as “mere mortal” because the emphasis in context is not on Peter’s maleness, but his humanity. Contrary to what Cornelius thought, Peter was not a god or an angelic being, but a mere mortal.

verses.zh: 彼得和他说着话进去，见有好些人在那里聚集，
verses.en: Peter[NOTE:1] continued talking with him as he went in, and he found many people gathered together.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “And he”; the referent (Peter) has been specified in the translation for clarity. Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Or “many people assembled.”

verses.zh: 就对他们说：「你们知道，犹太人和别国的人亲近来往本是不合例的，但　神已经指示我，无论甚么人都不可看作俗而不洁净的。
verses.en: He said to them, “You know that[NOTE:1] it is unlawful[NOTE:2] for a Jew[NOTE:3] to associate with or visit a Gentile,[NOTE:4] yet God has shown me that I should call no person[NOTE:5] defiled or ritually unclean.[NOTE:6]
notes: Here ὡς (hōs) is used like ὅτι (hoti) to introduce indirect discourse (cf. BDAG 1105 s.v. ὡς 5).
This term is used of wanton or callously lawless acts (BDAG 24 s.v. ἀθέμιτος).
Grk “a Jewish man” (ἀνδρὶ ᾿Ιουδαίῳ, andri Ioudaiō).

Grk “a foreigner,” but in this context, “a non-Jew,” that is, a Gentile. This term speaks of intimate association (BDAG 556 s.v. κολλάω 2.b.α). On this Jewish view, see John 18:28, where a visit to a Gentile residence makes a Jewish person unclean.
This is a generic use of ἄνθρωπος (anthrōpos).

Possibly there is a subtle distinction in meaning between κοινός (koinos) and ἀκάθαρτος (akathartos) here, but according to L&N 53.39 it is difficult to determine precise differences in meaning based on existing contexts.sn God has shown me…unclean. Peter sees the significance of his vision as not about food, but about open fellowship between Jewish Christians and Gentiles.

verses.zh: 所以我被请的时候，就不推辞而来。现在请问：你们叫我来有甚么意思呢？」
verses.en: Therefore when you sent for me,[NOTE:1] I came without any objection. Now may I ask why[NOTE:2] you sent for me?”
notes: Grk “Therefore when I was sent for.” The passive participle μεταπεμφθείς (metapemphtheis) has been taken temporally and converted to an active construction which is less awkward in English.
Grk “ask for what reason.”

verses.zh: 哥尼流说：「前四天，这个时候，我在家中守着申初的祷告，忽然有一个人穿着光明的衣裳，站在我面前，
verses.en: Cornelius[NOTE:1] replied,[NOTE:2] “Four days ago at this very hour, at three o’clock in the afternoon,[NOTE:3] I was praying in my house, and suddenly[NOTE:4] a man in shining clothing stood before me
notes: Grk “And Cornelius.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Grk “said.”
Grk “at the ninth hour.” Again, this is the hour of afternoon prayer.

Grk “and behold.” The interjection ἰδού (idou) is difficult at times to translate into English. Here it has been translated as “suddenly” to convey the force of Cornelius’ account of the angel’s appearance.

verses.zh: 说：『哥尼流，你的祷告已蒙垂听，你的周济达到　神面前已蒙记念了。
verses.en: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard and your acts of charity[NOTE:1] have been remembered before God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “your gifts to the needy.”
This statement is a paraphrase rather than an exact quotation of Acts 10:4.

verses.zh: 你当打发人往约帕去，请那称呼彼得的西门来，他住在海边一个硝皮匠西门的家里。』
verses.en: Therefore send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. This man is staying as a guest in the house of Simon the tanner,[NOTE:1] by the sea.’
notes: Or “with a certain Simon Berseus.” Although most modern English translations treat βυρσεῖ (bursei) as Simon’s profession (“Simon the tanner”), it is possible that the word is actually Simon’s surname (“Simon Berseus” or “Simon Tanner”). BDAG 185 s.v. βυρσεύς regards it as a surname.

verses.zh: 所以我立时打发人去请你。你来了很好；现今我们都在　神面前，要听主所吩咐你的一切话。」
verses.en: Therefore I sent for you at once, and you were kind enough to come.[NOTE:1] So now we are all here in the presence of God[NOTE:2] to listen[NOTE:3] to everything the Lord has commanded you to say to us.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “you have done well by coming.” The idiom καλῶς ποιεῖν (kalōs poiein) is translated “be kind enough to do someth.” by BDAG 505-6 s.v. καλῶς 4.a. The participle παραγενόμενος (paragenomenos) has been translated as an English infinitive due to the nature of the English idiom (“kind enough to” + infinitive).
The translation “we are here in the presence of God” for ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πάρεσμεν (enōpion tou theou paresmen) is given by BDAG 773 s.v. πάρειμι 1.a.
Or “to hear everything.”
The words “to say to us” are not in the Greek text, but are implied. Cornelius knows Peter is God’s representative, bringing God’s message.

verses.zh: 彼得就开口说：「我真看出　神是不偏待人。
verses.en: Then Peter started speaking:[NOTE:1] “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism in dealing with people,[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “Opening his mouth Peter said” (a Semitic idiom for beginning to speak in a somewhat formal manner). The participle ἀνοίξας (anoixas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.

Grk “God is not one who is a respecter of persons,” that is, “God is not one to show partiality” (cf. BDAG 887 s.v. προσωπολήμπτης). L&N 88.239 translates this verse “I realize that God does not show favoritism (in dealing with people).” The underlying Hebrew idiom includes the personal element (“respecter of persons”) so the phrase “in dealing with people” is included in the present translation. It fits very well with the following context and serves to emphasize the relational component of God’s lack of partiality. The latter is a major theme in the NT: Rom 2:11; Eph 2:11-22; Col 3:25; Jas 2:1; 1 Pet 1:17. This was the lesson of Peter’s vision.

verses.zh: 原来，各国中那敬畏主、行义的人都为主所悦纳。
verses.en: but in every nation[NOTE:1] the person who fears him[NOTE:2] and does what is right[NOTE:3] is welcomed before him.
notes: See Luke 24:47.
Or “shows reverence for him.”

Grk “works righteousness”; the translation “does what is right” for this phrase in this verse is given by L&N 25.85.sn Note how faith and response are linked here by the phrase and does what is right.

verses.zh: 神藉着耶稣基督（他是万有的主）传和平的福音，将这道赐给以色列人。
verses.en: You know[NOTE:1] the message[NOTE:2] he sent to the people[NOTE:3] of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace[NOTE:4] through[NOTE:5] Jesus Christ[NOTE:6] (he is Lord[NOTE:7] of all)—
notes: The subject and verb (“you know”) do not actually occur until the following verse, but have been repeated here because of the requirements of English word order.
Grk “the word.”
Grk “to the sons.”
Peace is a key OT concept: Isa 52:7; Nah 1:15; also for Luke: Luke 1:79; 2:14; Acts 9:31. See also the similar phrase in Eph 2:17.
Or “by.”
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”
He is Lord of all. Though a parenthetical remark, this is the theological key to the speech. Jesus is Lord of all, so the gospel can go to all. The rest of the speech proclaims Jesus’ authority.

verses.zh: 这话在约翰宣传洗礼以后，从加利利起，传遍了犹太。
verses.en: you know what happened throughout Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism that John announced:[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “proclaimed.”

verses.zh: 神怎样以圣灵和能力膏拿撒勒人耶稣，这都是你们知道的。他周流四方，行善事，医好凡被魔鬼压制的人，因为　神与他同在。
verses.en: with respect to Jesus from Nazareth,[NOTE:1] that[NOTE:2] God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power. He[NOTE:3] went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil[NOTE:4] because God was with him.[NOTE:5]
notes: The somewhat awkward naming of Jesus as from Nazareth here is actually emphatic. He is the key subject of these key events.
Or “how.” The use of ὡς (hōs) as an equivalent to ὅτι (hoti) to introduce indirect or even direct discourse is well documented. BDAG 1105 s.v. ὡς 5 lists Acts 10:28 in this category.

Grk “power, who.” The relative pronoun was replaced by the pronoun “he,” and a new sentence was begun in the translation at this point to improve the English style, due to the length of the sentence in Greek.

The translation “healing all who were oppressed by the devil” is given in L&N 22.22.sn All who were oppressed by the devil. Note how healing is tied to the cosmic battle present in creation. Christ’s power overcomes the devil and his forces, which seek to destroy humanity.
See Acts 7:9.

verses.zh: 他在犹太人之地，并耶路撒冷所行的一切事，有我们作见证。他们竟把他挂在木头上杀了。
verses.en: We[NOTE:1] are witnesses of all the things he did both in Judea[NOTE:2] and in Jerusalem.[NOTE:3] They[NOTE:4] killed him by hanging him on a tree,[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “And we.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Grk “the land of the Jews,” but this is similar to the phrase used as the name of the province of Judea in 1 Macc 8:3 (see BDAG 1093-94 s.v. χώρα 2.b).
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Grk “in Jerusalem, whom they killed.” The relative pronoun was replaced by the pronoun “him” and a new sentence was begun in the translation at this point to improve the English style, due to the length of the sentence in Greek.

Or “by crucifying him” (“hang on a tree” is by the time of the 1st century an idiom for crucifixion). The allusion is to the judgment against Jesus as a rebellious figure, appealing to the language of Deut 21:23. The Jewish leadership has badly “misjudged” Jesus.

verses.zh: 第三日，　神叫他复活，显现出来；
verses.en: but[NOTE:1] God raised him up on the third day and caused him to be seen,[NOTE:2]
notes: The conjunction “but” is not in the Greek text, but the contrast is clearly implied in the context. This is technically asyndeton, or lack of a connective, in Greek.
Grk “and granted that he should become visible.” The literal Greek idiom is somewhat awkward in English. L&N 24.22 offers the translation “caused him to be seen” for this verse.

verses.zh: 不是显现给众人看，乃是显现给　神预先所拣选为他作见证的人看，就是我们这些在他从死里复活以后和他同吃同喝的人。
verses.en: not by all the people, but by us, the witnesses God had already chosen,[NOTE:1] who ate and drank[NOTE:2] with him after he rose from the dead.
notes: Or “the witnesses God had previously chosen.” See Acts 1:8.
Ate and drank. See Luke 24:35-49.

verses.zh: 他吩咐我们传道给众人，证明他是　神所立定的，要作审判活人、死人的主。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] commanded us to preach to the people and to warn[NOTE:2] them[NOTE:3] that he is the one[NOTE:4] appointed[NOTE:5] by God as judge[NOTE:6] of the living and the dead.
notes: Grk “and he.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.

The verb διαμαρτύρομαι (diamarturomai) can mean “warn,” and such a meaning is highly probable in this context where a reference to the judgment of both the living and the dead is present. The more general meaning “to testify solemnly” does not capture this nuance.
The word “them” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.
Grk “that this one is the one,” but this is awkward in English and has been simplified to “that he is the one.”
Or “designated.” BDAG 723 s.v. ὁρίζω 2.b has “the one appointed by God as judge” for this phrase.
Jesus has divine authority as judge over the living and the dead: Acts 17:26-31; Rom 14:9; 1 Thess 5:9-10; 1 Tim 4:1; 1 Pet 4:5.

verses.zh: 众先知也为他作见证说：『凡信他的人必因他的名得蒙赦罪。』」
verses.en: About him all the prophets testify,[NOTE:1] that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins[NOTE:2] through his name.”
notes: Or “All the prophets testify about him.” Although modern English translations tend to place “about him” after “testify” (so NIV, NRSV) the phrase “about him” has been left at the beginning of v. 43 for emphatic reasons.
Forgiveness of sins. See Luke 24:47; also Acts 14:23; 19:4; 9:42; 11:17; 16:31. The gospel is present in the prophetic promise, Rom 1:1-7. The message is in continuity with the ancient hope.

verses.zh: 彼得还说这话的时候，圣灵降在一切听道的人身上。
verses.en: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell on[NOTE:1] all those who heard the message.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “came down on.” God now acted to confirm the point of Peter’s speech.
Or “word.”

verses.zh: 那些奉割礼、和彼得同来的信徒，见圣灵的恩赐也浇在外邦人身上，就都希奇；
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] circumcised believers[NOTE:2] who had accompanied Peter were greatly astonished[NOTE:3] that[NOTE:4] the gift of the Holy Spirit[NOTE:5] had been poured out[NOTE:6] even on the Gentiles,
notes: Grk “And the.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Or “The Jewish Christians”; Grk “The believers from the circumcision.”

The Jewish Christians who were with Peter were greatly astonished because they thought the promise of the Spirit would be limited only to those of Israel. God’s plan was taking on fresh dimensions even as it was a reflection of what the prophets had promised.
Or “because.”
That is, the gift consisting of the Holy Spirit. Here τοῦ πνεύματος (tou pneumatos) is a genitive of apposition; the gift consists of the Spirit.
The gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out. Cf. the account in Acts 2, especially 2:33. Note also Joel 2:17-21 and Acts 11:15-18.

verses.zh: 因听见他们说方言，称赞　神为大。
verses.en: for they heard them speaking in tongues and praising[NOTE:1] God. Then Peter said,
notes: Or “extolling,” “magnifying.”

verses.zh: 于是彼得说：「这些人既受了圣灵，与我们一样，谁能禁止用水给他们施洗呢？」
verses.en: “No one can withhold the water for these people to be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit just as we did,[NOTE:1] can he?”[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “just as also we.” The auxiliary verb in English must be supplied. This could be either “have” (NIV, NRSV) or “did” (NASB). “Did” is preferred here because the comparison Peter is making concerns not just the fact of the present possession of the Spirit (“they received the Spirit we now possess”), but the manner in which the Gentiles in Cornelius’ house received the Spirit (“they received the Spirit in the same manner we did [on the day of Pentecost]”).

The Greek construction anticipates a negative reply which is indicated in the translation by the ‘tag’ question, “can he?” The question is rhetorical. Peter was saying these Gentiles should be baptized since God had confirmed they were his.

verses.zh: 就吩咐奉耶稣基督的名给他们施洗。他们又请彼得住了几天。
verses.en: So he gave orders to have them baptized[NOTE:1] in the name of Jesus Christ.[NOTE:2] Then they asked him to stay for several days.
notes: The Greek construction (passive infinitive with accusative subject) could be translated either “he ordered them to be baptized” or “he ordered that they be baptized,” but the implication in English in either case is that Peter was giving orders to the Gentiles in Cornelius’ house, telling them to get baptized. It is much more likely in the context that Peter was ordering those Jewish Christians who accompanied him to baptize the new Gentile converts. They would doubtless have still had misgivings even after witnessing the outpouring of the Spirit and hearing the tongues. It took Peter’s apostolic authority (“ordered”) to convince them to perform the baptisms.
Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.” Jesus’ right to judge as the provider of forgiveness is highlighted here.
